content.comment_body: Hello, Let me introduce my situation. Our family operates a small business in energy production. A collaborator who manages a related company handed me a project involving a basic PLC program for a small hydroplant. This program only measures dam water level and turbine RPM, and allows for basic control like start, stop, and power adjustment. The person who initially helped create the program hasn't finished it, so we're likely restarting. My experience with PLC programming is limited, mostly dating back to a brief course years ago on Mitsubishi systems. Although I'm comfortable with computers, after several days trying to work through this, I've found myself frustrated and confused, even considering removing all related software and hardware out of frustration. --- I have a standard starter kit that includes a [product_name] module, a [product_name] operator panel, and the accompanying software. Despite this kit being marketed as beginner-friendly, I haven't managed to get these two units to communicate at all. I'm looking for a step-by-step guide—preferably something extremely basic—on how to get from zero knowledge up to where the [product_name] and the [product_name] operator panel can communicate. Is anyone able to assist with these seemingly fundamental steps, or at least clarify why the PLC kits come packaged with software that doesn't seem fully compatible with the hardware or available tutorials? Thanks in advance for any help or advice. Sorry for the length of this post. Best regards, [user_name]

You might be overestimating the forum's scope. This space is mainly intended for help with specific problems, not as a substitute for a full training course. If you have detailed questions, feel free to ask, and we can assist.

You haven't stated precisely which [product_name] module, including its [article_no], or which versions of [product_name] and the software you are using. Without that info, I can't create a tailored example for you. To achieve basic communication between the [product_name] module and the operator panel, you only need to set up a connection in the software for the operator panel. There's no need to configure anything additional on the [product_name] module side.

I disagree with your perspective. When buying a car, for instance, it's important to find out beforehand what features it has and what you need, like knowing you'll need a key to start it. Similarly, a starter kit offers several components at a reduced price, but isn't designed as a learning package. All required software for programming is included, and when purchasing programmable devices, it's assumed you will do the programming yourself.
Don't take this the wrong way. The forum is here to help, but it's not realistic to convey substantial knowledge in just one or two posts.

Keep in mind, those assisting here are volunteers. The forum cannot replace professional training services offered by [company_name] and its partners. That said, @ixo65: Is there a sample project provided by [company_name] that demonstrates the hardware in the starter kit, specifically linking the [product_name] module and the operator panel? Thank you in advance.

There are two main methods to connect a [product_name] module to an operator panel from [company_name]: 1. Through an HMI connection. The [product_name] module supports only one HMI connection, so you must configure a connection in both devices. This method is standard since [product_name] V11.x (using the software platform). 2. Using an S7 connection, which only requires configuration on the operator panel. Currently, [company_name] doesn't offer an official example for this setup, but it is my preferred approach.

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge for users is finding beginner-friendly resources for connecting a [product_name] PLC module and an operator panel using [company_name] software. Users expected the starter kit to facilitate straightforward integration, but instead, software compatibility and a steep learning curve make the process difficult for newcomers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that the starter kit—with both software and hardware—should be intuitive, fully compatible, and supported by clear tutorials or documentation that guide complete beginners through making essential connections.
